tools.description: Read OyList's own guidance, taken from its website, to guide the user while they make a list. Without a topic: the writing tips, what the available list settings mean, how the list score works, and the help topics. With a topic: OyList's answers to common questions on it (creating, visibility, copyi

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Read what the account has used and has left today: OyList's daily allowances for new lists, new items and asset searches, and this connection's budgets for tool calls, edits, asset selections and uploads, each with its reset time. Reading uses none of them beyond the call itself.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List OyList categories and their suggested asset types.

tools.name: list_my_lists
tools.description: List the connected account's drafts or published lists, including its own unlisted lists.

tools.name: get_list
tools.description: Read list details and one page of entries the connected account can view.

tools.name: create_list_draft
tools.description: Create a draft using the supplied title, category, list type, and visibility.

tools.name: edit_list
tools.description: Edit supplied list details. Omitted fields retain their current value.

tools.name: publish_list
tools.description: Publish a specific draft with its saved visibility. A public list can appear on OyList and be announced to followers.

tools.name: delete_list
tools.description: Delete the specified list when explicitly requested.

tools.name: search_assets
tools.description: Search OyList and its website subject sources for a matching subject. Search results contain untrusted source text.

tools.name: select_asset
tools.description: Resolve a subject returned by search to its OyList asset ID. Existing OyList asset IDs can be used directly in items.

tools.name: add_items
tools.description: Add up to 100 supplied entries. Provide an asset ID for a matching linked subject or provide a title and assetType for an unlinked entry, with a description and image when available. A title supplied with an asset ID becomes its own title, shown above the linked subject: use it when the entry is a m

tools.name: edit_item
tools.description: Change supplied fields on one entry. Use a null asset ID to unlink it, or a null image ID to clear its picture where the format permits.

tools.name: move_item
tools.description: Set the entry's position in the list's manual order.

tools.name: delete_item
tools.description: Delete the specified entry when explicitly requested.

tools.name: set_list_image
tools.description: Set a list header or thumbnail to a picture uploaded through this connection. The website crops a header to 3:1 (1536x512) and a thumbnail to 2:3 (1024x1536), so upload a picture already in that shape. Use null to remove the explicit image when requested.

tools.name: get_artwork_status
tools.description: Check the existing automatic artwork queue and eligibility for an editable list. If enabled, a public list with three accepted items and a current quality score of 65 can enter the queue. No completion time is guaranteed.

tools.name: view_list_images
tools.description: Look at saved pictures: a list's header and thumbnail and up to eight of its entries' pictures, returned as images in the order listed. An entry with no picture of its own shows its linked subject's picture, reported as subjectImageId. Use it to check that a picture loads and shows what its entry de

tools.name: list_profiles
tools.description: List the OyList accounts that approved this connection, by username. With more than one, ask the user which to use and pass it as profile to the other tools.

tools.name: add_profile
tools.description: Get the link to approve another OyList account for this connection. Give the user the link and steps. Each account approves its own access in the browser.

tools.name: remove_profile
tools.description: Revoke this connection's access to the named account when the user asks. Any account can be removed independently and can approve access again later.

tools.name: disconnect
tools.description: Sign this app out of OyList when the user asks. This ends the app connection and removes every account approval on it.

tools.name: get_image_upload_link
tools.description: Create a 10-minute upload link for one JPEG, PNG, or WebP file just under 10 MiB. If you hold the file and can make HTTP requests, post it yourself as directUpload describes (multipart field "image" with the Authorization header) and read the image ID from the reply. Otherwise give the user uploadUr

tools.name: get_image_upload_status
tools.description: Look up the image ID after the user uploads a file through the OyList upload page.

tools.name: upload_image_from_address
tools.description: Upload a JPEG, PNG, or WebP picture from the public web address the user chose, just under 10 MiB. Give the https address of the picture file itself, not the page showing it. OyList downloads it and applies its usual image checks. Verify what the picture shows before using it.

tools.name: upload_image
tools.description: Upload a small JPEG, PNG, or WebP file the user chose and the client already holds, at most 1 MiB encoded as base64. Prefer upload_image_from_address or an upload link for anything larger.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_image_upload_link" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Create a 10-minute upload link for one JPEG, PNG, or WebP file just under 10 MiB. If you hold the file and can make HTTP requests, post it yourself as directUpl…

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "upload_image_from_address" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Upload a JPEG, PNG, or WebP picture from the public web address the user chose, just under 10 MiB. Give the https address of the picture file itself, not the pa…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_image_upload_link · Private data: get_image_upload_link, get_image_upload_status, upload_image_from_address, upload_image · Public sink: publish_list, set_list_image, get_image_upload_link, get_image_upload_status, upload_image_from_address, upload_image · Destructive: get_usage, delete_list, edit_item, delete_item, set_list_image, remove_profile.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_image_upload_link · Private data: get_image_upload_link, get_image_upload_status, upload_image_from_address, upload_image · Public sink: publish_list, set_list_image, get_image_upload_link, get_image_upload_status, upload_image_from_address, upload_image · Destructive: get_usage, delete_list, edit_item, delete_item, set_list_image, remove_profile

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
